work.title: String Quartet in C major, Op. 54 No. 2

version.note: The performing edition and any editorial choices are not identified in the recording sources. The performance appears to omit the first-movement exposition repeat, which is an observation from the audio, not a documented fact.

performers.note: The Commons file and the video name the ensemble only. The individual players of this 2015 concert are not listed in the sources consulted, so no names are inferred.

date.note: The uploader’s video description gives the concert as May 2015. The Commons date, 24 July 2015, is the YouTube upload date, not a session date.

place.value: Tel Aviv Museum of Art, Tel Aviv, Israel
place.note: Stated in the video description. The video is titled “Haydn Quartet Op. 54 No. 2, Danish String Quartet LIVE”; the description misprints the opus as 64.

label.note: A born-digital concert video: there is no commercial disc or tape carrier.

catalogue.note: No catalogue number applies to a concert video upload.

matrixTakeSides.note: No matrix, take or side applies to a born-digital concert video.

credits.note: The video description credits Gilad Shabani for the video and Ilan Rechtman as music director of the concert series; neither is credited for extracting the audio. A Commons uploader’s username is not a transfer credit.

date.note: No transfer date is documented; the Commons date 2015-07-24 is the YouTube upload date.

processing.value: Audio taken from the YouTube concert video and stored on Commons as an Ogg Vorbis file, which Commons transcodes to an MP3 derivative.
processing.note: The Commons file is one of four movement extracts from a single 19-minute video; who made the cuts, and whether any editing or loudness processing was applied, is not stated.

digital.format: MP3 access derivative supplied by Wikimedia Commons; uploaded source: Ogg Vorbis

composition.value: Underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies.
composition.note: Haydn died in 1809. This is a term calculation, not a worldwide clearance or a statement about an unidentified modern edition.

recording.value: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 (the Commons {{YouTube CC-BY}} template): an explicit release of the recording for any use with attribution.
recording.note: This is rule 1 of the programme’s rights rule, an explicit recording release. The Commons file page records the YouTube CC-BY status of the source video. The sources do not show who applied that setting; it is taken to be the channel owner who posted the concert film, and it covers the video as posted.

rights.creditLine: Joseph Haydn, String Quartet in C major, Op. 54 No. 2, II. Adagio; The Danish String Quartet, live at the Tel Aviv Museum of Art, May 2015. Video credited to Gilad Shabani, concert series music director Ilan Rechtman. Via Wikimedia Commons from YouTube; Creative Commons Attribution 3.0.
